body.message: No speculative estimate is produced for Intel Corporation. It was refused a standard valuation because it loses money, and even a projected path to profitability does not apply to it. No figure is reported, deliberately.
reasons:
The company is loss-making: its day-to-day business lost $23m in its 2025 financial year, and it made a loss in 2 of the last 4 years.
    This kind of valuation assumes a business that already makes a profit and grows steadily. Applying it to a loss-making company would mean inventing the profits it then puts a value on.

Intel Corporation's revenue has fallen - -0.5% in the latest year and -5.7% a year over the period. This approach projects growth into profitability; a shrinking company offers no growth to extend, and assuming a reversal would invent it.

assumptions.name: speculative_revenue_growth
assumptions.detail: the lower of the latest year's revenue growth (-0.5%) and the 3-year CAGR (-5.7%), so an early ramp from a small base is not extrapolated; raw -5.7% clamped to [0%, 30%]

assumptions.name: target_operating_margin
assumptions.detail: a generic mature-company operating margin. It is not specific to this company or its industry, and the company has never earned it

assumptions.name: years_to_profitability
assumptions.detail: the distance from today's -0% operating margin to the 10% target, closed at 15 percentage points a year - a fast pace to sustain; 1 year(s) clamped to [2, 10]

assumptions.name: post_profitability_growth
assumptions.detail: half the 0.0% assumed until profitability, as growth slows with scale; floored at terminal growth

assumptions.name: mature_capex_pct
assumptions.detail: 5% of revenue, typical of a mature business - today's build-out rate of 40.0% is not assumed to last. Depreciation is assumed to equal capex once mature

assumptions.name: mature_nwc_pct
assumptions.detail: the company's working-capital investment of 0.0% of revenue growth

assumptions.name: tax_rate
assumptions.detail: US statutory rate. A loss-maker's tax history says nothing about a profitable future, and accumulated tax losses that would shelter early profits are not credited, which errs low

assumptions.name: wacc
assumptions.detail: CAPM: 5.01% + 2.37x5.50% = 18.05% equity; debt 2.00% (2.00% after tax); weights 92.0%E / 8.0%D

assumptions.name: terminal_growth
assumptions.detail: global default (~long-run nominal GDP growth), shared with the DCF

assumptions.name: projection_years
assumptions.detail: years of mature-company forecast after profitability, before the terminal value

body.disclaimer: THIS IS NOT A VALUATION, AND IT IS NOT AN ESTIMATE OF WHAT INTEL CORPORATION IS WORTH. It is arithmetic on assumptions you typed in. Intel Corporation loses money and was refused a standard valuation; it was then refused a speculative estimate as well, because its own figures show no path to profitability to project. Nothing here is derived from the company's data: you have assumed revenue grows +8.0% a year and that the operating margin reaches 15% from -0.0% today within 5 years, and the figure below is what those assumptions imply. Intel Corporation's revenue is actually falling 5.7% a year, so this figure assumes a reversal the company's own figures do not show. Change any one of them and it moves by multiples or changes sign. Treat it as a way of seeing what your own beliefs would have to be worth, not as information about the company, and never as a reason to buy or sell.
